gloss: to come to a dead end; to reach an impasse

definitions.gloss: to come to a dead end; to reach a dead end
definitions.explanation: To reach a point where a road, path, or passage ends and one cannot go further.

definitions.gloss: to reach an impasse; to be stuck
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to reach a point where no further progress can be made in a plan, investigation, or negotiation.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{行|い}き{止|ど}まる。
examples.english: This road comes to a dead end.

examples.japanese: {細|ほそ}い{路地|ろじ}を{進|すす}んだら{壁|かべ}の{前|まえ}で{行|い}き{止|ど}まった。
examples.english: I went down a narrow alley and came to a dead end at a wall.

examples.japanese: カーナビの{案内|あんない}に{従|したが}ったのに、{山道|やまみち}で{行|い}き{止|ど}まってしまった。
examples.english: I followed the car navigation but ended up at a dead end on a mountain road.

examples.japanese: {調査|ちょうさ}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まった。
examples.english: The investigation hit a dead end.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}は{完全|かんぜん}に{行|い}き{止|ど}まっている。
{研究|けんきゅう}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まったとき、まったく{別|べつ}の{角度|かくど}からアプローチしてみた。
examples.english: When the research reached an impasse, I tried approaching it from a completely different angle.

notes:
A compound verb from {行|い}く (to go) and {止|と}まる (to stop). The related noun {行|い}き{止|ど}まり (dead end) is extremely common and appears on road signs throughout Japan.

USAGE:
- Intransitive verb — the subject is the road, path, investigation, etc.
- The noun form {行|い}き{止|ど}まり is more common in everyday use than the verb
- Often seen on road signs: {行|い}き{止|ど}まり (Dead End)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道|みち}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まる: the road comes to a dead end
- {捜査|そうさ}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まる: the investigation hits a dead end
- {交渉|こうしょう}が{行|い}き{止|ど}まる: negotiations stall
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まりの{道|みち}: a dead-end road

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まる: to be stuck, to reach a deadlock — emphasizes being completely blocked with no way forward; stronger and more commonly figurative
- {行|い}き{止|ど}まり: dead end (noun) — the noun form, used on signs and in directions
- {立|た}ち{往生|おうじょう}する: to be stranded, to be stuck — unable to move (often vehicles or people)
